old: پشتِ امپدانسِ دیده‌شده از جای خطا.
new: پشتِ امپدانسِ دیده‌شده از جای خطا. اگر $S_	ext{sc}$ همان توانِ اتصالِ کوتاهِ اعلام‌شدهٔ بهره‌بردار ($S''_	ext{kQ}$) باشد، [STD-131]{.ltr} امپدانسِ شبکه را $c\,U_	ext{n}^2/S''_	ext{kQ}$ می‌گیرد و جریانِ خطا در خودِ نقطهٔ اتصال همان [6.56 kA]{.ltr} می‌ماند (@exm-ch28-thevenin)؛ مدلِ آموزشیِ این فصل امپدانس را $U_	ext{n}^2/S_	ext{sc}$ می‌سازد و $c$ را روی آن می‌گذارد، پس جریان‌های بیشینهٔ این بخش حدودِ ۱۰ درصد محافظه‌کارانه‌اند.
why: In IEC 60909-0 the network feeder impedance is Z_Q = c U_n^2 / S''_kQ, so the operator-given short-circuit power already contains c; the chapter builds Z = U^2/S_sc and then multiplies by c = 1.1, so the POC maximum fault current is 7.21/7.22 kA here but 6.56 kA in the same chapter's Thevenin table for the same 1,500 MVA. The convention (and its ~10 % conservatism) must be stated, or the model changed.
evidence: a_thevenin.txt: 'max 1500 ... I_k kA 6.56'; b_sc.txt: 'POC 132 7.21'; vershi 1.1 x 1500/(sqrt3 x 132) = 7.22; IEC 60909-0:2016 eq. for network feeder Z_Q = c_Q U_nQ^2 / S''_kQ (also the min case c=1.0 reproduces 3.94 = 900/(sqrt3*132), only the max case double-counts). Same issue in y-plantp exm-ch28-int-1 (7.22 vs 7.21) and exr-ch28-46 ('with and without c').

why: plantp/gridstudy.py fault_current() and the ch 28 source model (companion/ch28/sources.py GRID s_sc used as Z = 1/s_sc in pu) apply c = 1.1 on a source impedance built without c. Per IEC 60909-0 build the grid source as z = c_max / s_sc (pu) for the maximum case (and c_min / s_sc for the minimum) and keep the voltage source c, or equivalently drop c for the grid part; then the POC grid contribution becomes 6.56 kA (not 7.21) and b_sc.txt, int_hand.txt and the figure ch28-faults change by about -9 %. Alternatively keep the code and add the convention note of TJ-01.
evidence: gridstudy.py lines 132-143: i_grid = c / z_kk with z_kk from 1/s_sc; a_thevenin.txt prints 6.56 kA for the same source.

why: The output gives 0.67 % (max) and 1.11 % (min) per 10 Mvar: a factor 1.66, not 'doubles'; the WSCR does not enter that column.

With delta = 0.863 the external insulation is 1 - 0.863 = 13.7 % weaker; 16 % is the extra strength needed (1/delta = 1.159). The companion output examples_y.py (y_altitude.txt, 'about 16 % weaker than at sea level') has the same slip: change it to 'about 14 % weaker (chosen 16 % stronger)'.

new: ولتاژهای تماس و گام فقط در لحظهٔ خطا وجود دارند و زمانِ رخ‌دادنِ خطا پیش‌بینی‌شدنی نیست.
why: Touch and step voltages are calculable (the section itself computes GPR and body currents, and the earthing-guide method of IEEE 80 predicts them); what cannot be predicted is when the fault happens. As written the warning contradicts the section and suggests design calculation is futile.
evidence: Same section: eq-ch26-gpr, exm-ch26-body; IEEE Std 80-2013 computes mesh and step voltages from grid geometry.
